system.name: DriveSense Lane & Object Perception
system.intended_purpose: Detect lane boundaries, vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists from forward camera and radar to support an SAE Level 2 driver-assistance feature.
system.deployment_context: Embedded automotive SoC; real-time perception at 30Hz feeding the ADAS planning stack.

governance.oversight: Level 2 system requires a continuously attentive driver; driver-monitoring enforces hands-on and gaze and disengages the feature on non-response.

out_of_scope: Operation outside the validated operational design domain (no off-road, no unmapped construction zones)
risks: Missed detection of vulnerable road users in low light or glare
False lane detection on worn or ambiguous markings
Sensor degradation from occlusion (mud, snow, direct sun)

metrics: VRU recall in low-light ODD slice: 0.81
measure.test_data: 1,100 hours of geo-diverse driving log replay plus a SOTIF edge-case scenario catalogue, partitioned by ODD condition (lighting, weather, road type).
measure.fairness: Pedestrian recall evaluated across skin-tone proxy bins and child-vs-adult stature to surface detection disparities; gaps tracked in the SOTIF triage log.

mitigations: Radar-camera sensor fusion with degraded-mode fallback
Conservative time-to-collision thresholds in low-confidence conditions
ODD exit triggers graceful handback to the driver
manage.monitoring: Fleet shadow-mode disengagement and near-miss telemetry reviewed weekly; field-monitoring per ISO 21448 with OTA-gated rollouts.
